ca_baskerville_rock.blurb: Baskerville Rock is a freestanding granite formation in the Quail Springs part of Joshua Tree National Park, a short stroll from the day-use area. It holds a dozen climbs, almost all of them gear-protected cracks and faces, with a pair of top-rope lines. The range runs from beginner-level scrambles up to a single 5.11, but most routes sit between 5.9 and 5.10, so it suits climbers who already place their own protection. The wall faces northeast, so the base catches morning light while the rock keeps some shade through the day. Its best-known line is a steady 5.10 hand crack.

ca_jimmy_cliff_east_face.blurb: The east side of Jimmy Cliff is a small single-pitch wall on the outer edge of the Lost Horse area in Joshua Tree. Of its dozen routes, eight are trad leads and four are set up as top ropes, with no sport climbing. Difficulty clusters in the 5.10 range, with a few 5.9s, one 5.8 and a single 5.11, so it works best for climbers comfortable on moderate to stout gear routes. Pitches are short, around 60 feet, and the face points east. The top-outs can be reached by rappel or a walk-off around the north end of the west side.

ca_2_mystery_tower.blurb: Mystery Tower is the second wall you meet on the way into the Marble Caves, a limestone sport crag perched well over the Trinity River's South Fork in far northern California. All twelve routes are bolted, running from one 5.8 up through a solid block of 5.11s and a slightly bigger group of 5.12s, so it is mainly a wall for strong leaders. The face is steep and fairly long, with a leaning ramp crossing it, and it picks up full sun from around late morning. The wider cliff sees few visitors, which makes for a quiet day.

ca_mt_russell.blurb: Mt. Russell is a 14,086-foot High Sierra peak right beside Mt. Whitney, tucked out of view until you are fairly close. Nearly all of its routes are alpine, with one trad line. The easiest way up is the long East Ridge, a third-class outing, while the steep faces and arete carry technical multi-pitch climbs. Grades run from scrambling through 5.6 and 5.8 to a handful of 5.9s and a group of 5.10s, with the best-known arete line around 5.9. Expect a committed mountain day at high elevation, best for acclimatized parties.

ca_6_middle_aged_wall.blurb: Middle Aged Wall is a set of blocks and small towers just left of the main wall at the Pie Shop, on Lake Tahoe's South Shore. Most of its dozen routes are bolted, with a couple of trad lines and one top rope. Difficulty is broad: a gentle 5.5 for beginners, several climbs in the 5.8 to 5.9 band, and a handful of harder 5.10 to 5.12 lines. The face is sunny, so it is a pleasant pick when the shade elsewhere is cold, and the routes are short. Homes sit close by, so keep noise down.

ca_buttermilk_stem_boulder.blurb: Buttermilk Stem Boulder is a small cluster of blocks in the heart of the Buttermilks hillside outside Bishop, sitting midway from the Cave Area to the Tut Boulder. It carries a dozen problems from VB through V9, with a lot of the weight at the harder end: a few moderate V1 and V2 lines, then several V4 to V9 problems, many of them sit starts. The namesake V1 is a famous classic that draws a steady line of climbers. Landings in the Buttermilks are generally flat and sandy, and the boulders sit near the road, so it is easy to fit into a day of circuit hopping.
